title: In a 93-year-old scientific society's history, only three Indians had ever been inducted as Fellows. In 2026, the third one was a woman.

sources.text: YourStory Tamil - Physicist Kuljeet Kaur Marhas becomes first Indian woman Fellow at the Meteoritical Society
Kerala Kaumudi - Kuljeet Kaur Marhas, first Indian woman Fellow, Meteoritical Society

caption:
In a 93-year-old scientific society's history, only three Indians had ever been inducted as Fellows. In 2026, the third one was a woman.

She became the first Indian woman to receive the honour since the society's founding in 1933 and only the third Indian scientist overall, following Devendra Lal and J.N. Goswami.

Based at the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad, her research examines Calcium-Aluminium-rich Inclusions - some of the oldest solid material in the solar system - to understand how planets formed.

A 93-year-old international society inducting an Indian woman for the first time shows Indian fundamental research earning recognition on the same terms as the field's oldest institutions.
